prompt: A 'preview this link' feature lets users make the server fetch any URL.
tells: make the server fetch any URL
why: The server fetching user-chosen URLs can reach internal systems. That's SSRF.
trap: It's not the browser fetching; it's the server.

prompt: An attacker points the image importer at the cloud metadata endpoint and gets credentials.
why: SSRF reaches internal addresses like metadata services.
trap: Credentials leak, but the hole is the server-side fetch.

prompt: The webhook feature only allows fetching from an allow-list of hosts.
why: Allow-listing destinations is the main SSRF defence.
trap: It limits reach, but for URLs, not user rights.

prompt: Requesting http://localhost:8080/admin through the PDF generator opens an internal admin page.
why: The server was tricked into calling itself. SSRF.
trap: The admin page lacks checks too, but the way in is the fetch.

prompt: The URL passed the allow-list check, then redirected to an internal IP.
tells: then redirected to an internal IP
why: Following redirects can bypass SSRF checks. Re-check every hop.
trap: It looks like phishing, but the server is the victim.

prompt: A hostname resolved to a public IP during validation and a private IP when fetched.
why: DNS rebinding is an SSRF bypass. Validate the address you actually connect to.
trap: It involves DNS, but the attack is on server-side fetching.
